chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from Ibn Bint Ilyās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام say: If a woman dies while among men, and they do not find a woman to perform her ghusl, then some of the men should wash her from behind the clothes. And it is recommended that he wrap a cloth around his hands.

So this report bears two possibilities: one of them is that the man in question is her husband, for it is permissible for him to wash her as we have stated, from behind the clothes; or that he is one of her blood relatives, and that is reinforced by this.

key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهَا: to perform the ritual washing of her deceased body
key_terms.خِرْقَةً: a piece of cloth wrapped on the hands during washing
key_terms.ذَوِي أَرْحَامِهَا: her blood relatives/kin with close family relation
key_terms.زَوْجَهَا: her husband, who may have a distinct legal ruling
key_terms.مِنْ وَرَاءِ الثِّيَابِ: from behind the clothing, without direct exposure
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: it is recommended as a preferred practice

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased woman be given ghusl if no woman is present to wash her?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for washing a deceased woman when no woman is available and only unrelated men are present. It indicates that her body may be washed from behind clothing, with a cloth wrapped around the hands, and the accompanying discussion frames this within the cases of a husband or a mahram relative.
